root_cause.text: In `vsock_update_buffer_size()`, clamping the buffer size to `vsk->buffer_max_size` before clamping to `vsk->buffer_min_size` allows `vsk->buffer_size` to exceed `vsk->buffer_max_size` when the configured minimum is larger than the maximum, violating the intended socket memory boundary.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff shows the original order: first if `val > vsk->buffer_max_size` set to max, then if `val < vsk->buffer_min_size` set to min. The fix swaps these two checks to clamp to min first, then to max. The commit message explicitly states: "If a user sets a minimum buffer size larger than the maximum, the minimum check overrides the maximum check, inverting the constraint. This breaks the intended socket memory boundaries by allowing the vsk->buffer_size to grow beyond the configured vsk->buffer_max_size."

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix buffer size clamping order to enforce the maximum size constraint after the minimum, preventing the buffer size from exceeding the maximum in case of inconsistent min/max configuration.
intent_record.what: Swapped the order of two conditional checks that clamp the buffer size: first check against minimum, then against maximum.
intent_record.how: Previously, the buffer size was first capped to the maximum, then raised to the minimum. Now it is first raised to the minimum, then capped to the maximum. This ensures that the maximum constraint is applied last, so the final value cannot exceed the maximum even if the minimum is larger than the maximum.
